title: STANDING BETWEEN THE LIVING AND THE DEAD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: and the Lord said to Moses, "Get away from this assembly so I can put an end to them at once." And they fell facedown. Then Moses said to Aaron, "Take your censer and put incense in it, along with fire from the altar, and hurry to the assembly to make atonement for them. Wrath has come out from the Lord; the plague has started." So Aaron did as Moses said, and ran into the midst of the assembly. The plague had already started among the people, but Aaron offered the incense and made atonement for them. — Num 16:44-47 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The plague has begun, and God's people are dying. And what do Moses and Aaron do? They fall facedown once more, and then Aaron does something extraordinary — he takes his censer and runs straight into the midst of the dying crowd to make atonement for them. The priest runs toward the plague, not away from it, to save the very people who had just accused him of murder.

This is one of the most beautiful pictures of intercession in all of Scripture. Aaron does not stand at a safe distance. He plunges into the heart of the danger, placing himself between the wrath and the people, offering the incense that turns judgment aside. His love for the people overrides every reason to protect himself.

Think of what this cost him. These were the people who had grumbled against him, who had blamed him for God's judgment, who had made his life a burden. Yet Aaron risks everything to save them. This is love that overcomes offence, mercy that runs toward the undeserving. It is the heart of a true priest.

And how clearly this points us to Jesus, our great High Priest. Aaron ran into the midst of a dying people to make atonement; Jesus entered our dying world and took the plague of sin upon Himself. He did not stand at a safe distance from our danger — He plunged into the very heart of it, to the cross, to make atonement for those who had rebelled against Him. He placed Himself between us and the wrath we deserved. Aaron carried incense; Jesus carried His own blood. Our Priest ran toward us in our death to give us His life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you willing to intercede for those who have wronged you?
2. What does Aaron running toward the plague reveal about true love?
3. How does Jesus entering our danger to save us move your heart today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for Aaron who ran into the midst of a dying people to save them, and far more for Jesus, my great High Priest, who plunged into our death to make atonement. Give me a heart that intercedes with such love. Amen.
